title: Undercity
body: Beneath the broken capital of Lordaeron lies the Undercity, seat of the Forsaken. The old kingdom kept its royal crypts, catacombs, dungeons and sewers here, under the palace of its kings, and the poorest of its people lived in the gloom below. The Scourge began carving these depths into a stronghold, but Arthas left the work unfinished when he was called north. When Sylvanas Windrunner broke free and turned on the dreadlords who ruled the ruins, her Forsaken claimed the warren and finished it as their own. Lifts descend from the ruined palace to the Trade Quarter at its heart, ringed by the Magic Quarter, the Rogues' Quarter, the War Quarter and the Apothecarium, with foul canals running between them. Beyond lies the Royal Quarter, where the Dark Lady holds court.

parts.body: At her side stands the dreadlord Varimathras, one of three demon brothers who ruled Lordaeron's undead for the Burning Legion. When the Forsaken broke his forces he begged for his life and swore himself to her service, and he has served as her lieutenant ever since. The Deathstalkers, her elite agents, first served as his guard.

title: The Elevators
body: Three great lifts join the ruined palace of Lordaeron to the Trade Quarter far below, the main road between the open ruins and the city of the dead. They rise and fall without pause through long, dark shafts, and their doors close so quickly that the careless learn to step lively. Every traveler bound for the city's quarters, from the ruins above or the zeppelins beyond the walls, passes through them.

parts.body: When the Horde came to retake the city, the way down was closed to it. The rebels had wrecked the lift and trapped the shaft, and Sylvanas warned that a fall would mean certain death. Thrall answered by calling on the spirits of air, and cyclones lowered the Horde's champions safely into the inner sanctum below, where Khanok the Impassable barred their way.

title: Lady Sylvanas Windrunner
body: Once Ranger-General of Silvermoon, Sylvanas Windrunner fell defending Quel'Thalas from Arthas and was raised as a banshee in his service. When the Lich King's grip faltered she broke free, turned on the dreadlords who held Lordaeron and named her freed undead the Forsaken. She rules them from the Royal Quarter, curt with visitors, for the city does not run itself. She sends her chosen to Nathanos Blightcaller, one of her first champions, and few in her ranks serve her with more devotion.

parts.body: In recent years she has championed the blood elves of Quel'Thalas, once her own people, and stood for their entry into the Horde while others doubted them. Their envoys come before her throne in the Royal Quarter.

title: Varimathras
body: Varimathras was one of three dreadlord brothers who ruled Lordaeron's undead for the Burning Legion after Arthas went north. When Sylvanas broke his forces he begged for his life and offered his service, and for years he stood at her side in the Royal Quarter as her lieutenant, with the Deathstalkers first serving as his elite guard. His loyalty was a mask. After the Wrathgate he and Putress seized the Undercity, turning its halls into a fortress of demons and blight against the Horde.

parts.body: The Horde came for him through the fallen city, and he taunted it from the start: it would have its city back only in pieces. In the throne room, cornered by Thrall and Sylvanas, he opened portals for his demon kin, raged that years of tireless planning would not end like this, and begged a thousand-thousand pardons of an unseen Master, swearing to deal with the intruders himself. He could not. He fell with a last gasp: years, wasted.

title: Grand Apothecary Putress
body: Grand Apothecary Putress rose to the head of the Royal Apothecary Society after winning Sylvanas's favor with a vow to take the plague that made the Forsaken and make it their own weapon. From the Apothecarium his chemists refined the New Plague, a blight lethal to living and undead alike. At the Wrathgate in Northrend he turned it on Alliance, Horde and Scourge together, striking down Highlord Bolvar Fordragon and many soldiers of both sides. Then he went to ground in the depths of the Undercity, which traitors among the Forsaken had seized.

parts.body: To the Horde the betrayal cut deeper. Putress was the same apothecary credited with discovering the cure for the recent outbreak of the Scourge's plague, and he had not acted alone: with the dreadlord Varimathras he took the Undercity in a bloody coup, and those who would not side with them were executed or banished.
sources: quest 13257 reward text

parts.body: King Varian's forces broke into his laboratory in the Apothecarium, where blight generators fed him power. Cornered, Putress swore it would not end like this after so many years of work, swallowed ever more energy and raved that he saw everything. It availed him nothing. He died there, and Varian declared justice served.

title: Master Apothecary Faranell
body: Master Apothecary Faranell directs the work of the Royal Apothecary Society in the Apothecarium, overseeing its most ambitious and most ghoulish projects: guano from the bats of Razorfen Kraul, hearts cut from Scarlet zealots, venoms and composites sent home by his apothecaries in the field. He speaks of it all with unsettling delight, for every grisly reagent brings the Forsaken closer to the new plague the Dark Lady awaits.

parts.body: Since Putress's betrayal the Society labors under the eye of the Warchief's Kor'kron, and Faranell has turned diplomat. He assures his overseer that the apothecaries wish only to make amends for the tragic misguidance that ended so many lives, and to continue their research in peace. Putress, he insists, was an unfortunate anomaly.

title: Bragor Bloodfist
body: Bragor Bloodfist is a Kor'kron captain whom Thrall has sent to stand at the Dark Lady's side in the Royal Quarter. With most of the Forsaken army committed to Vengeance Landing in Northrend, the Warchief's guard now reinforces the Undercity, and Bragor sends agents against the Scarlet Crusade, receives word from the Hillsbrad front, and hunts a Scourge emissary named Malcin near Razorfen Downs. A living orc among the dead, he keeps dangerous books from the Forsaken as carefully as from the Shadow Council. He judges newcomers by their deeds, and already counts the human king among the threats the Horde must one day end.

parts.body: He came after the city was retaken. The fall of Varimathras left an empty place at the Dark Lady's side, and the Warchief filled it with one of his own: many duties the dreadlord once held, from the war on the Scarlet Crusade to the reports from Hillsbrad, now pass through Bragor's hands.

title: Overseer Kraggosh
body: Overseer Kraggosh is the Kor'kron orc posted inside the Apothecarium itself, and he makes no secret of how little he likes it. Since Putress loosed his blight at the Wrathgate, the Warchief has trusted the Royal Apothecary Society about as far as he could throw it, and Kraggosh is the result: no abomination guards, no secrecy, no plotting in the dark. The apothecaries can do nothing without him, and he has warned Master Apothecary Faranell that if the Society so much as spits without leave, the place will be shut down by force. His fellow overseers stand watch across the city and treat the Forsaken with open contempt.

title: Sharlindra
body: Sharlindra is a banshee of the Dark Lady's court and long in her service. She was present when Varimathras offered Sylvanas a place in his new order, and privately wondered whether accepting might have been the wiser course. She fought beside the Forsaken when they stormed the stronghold of the dreadlord Detheroc. Today she keeps to the Royal Quarter and directs agents abroad through lieutenants such as Melisara at Tarren Mill. When the ogre Mug'Thol stole the Crown of Will meant for Sylvanas, and the Dark Lady wanted an example made, it was Sharlindra who set the task in motion.

title: Parqual Fintallas
body: Before the plague took him, Parqual Fintallas was a great historian of Lordaeron's human kingdom. Death has not cured him of scholarship. He lingers in the Undercity still seeking enlightenment, though of a different kind, and holds that knowledge of the world will outlast mere strength. To those who would prove their minds he sets a final test of lore, sending them first to the Scarlet Monastery for a book its zealots once used to train paladins against his kind. His question, fittingly, concerns the very creature that became the Lich King and spread the plague across Lordaeron.

title: Apothecary Zinge
body: Apothecary Zinge of the Royal Apothecary Society has a sharp eye for opportunity, especially other people's. By her account Apothecary Keever, at work in the next room, is touched in the head, yet his research might bear fruit if pursued by a clever researcher, and Zinge means to be that researcher. She sends her errand runners to Alessandro Luca of Blue Moon Odds and Ends, who pines for her company, and on to the Tanaris desert to test the flesh of basilisks, scorpids and hyenas. She rewards those who stay useful, and corresponds with colleagues as far afield as the Crossroads and Kargath.

title: The Battle for the Undercity
body: At the Wrathgate in Northrend, Grand Apothecary Putress turned his blight on Alliance, Horde and Scourge alike, and Highlord Bolvar Fordragon fell with many soldiers of both sides. The treachery did not end there. Traitors within the Forsaken rose and seized the Undercity, and the Horde lost the capital of its ally, while Putress himself hid somewhere in its depths. Thrall has sworn that the perpetrators of this unforgivable crime will be brought to justice, and prepares to lay siege to the fallen city. Those who fought side by side at the Wrathgate are each left to count their dead.

parts.body: Thrall named the traitors: Putress, and with him the dreadlord Varimathras, the Dark Lady's own lieutenant. Those who would not side with their regime were executed or banished, Sylvanas herself was nearly killed, and the Forsaken who escaped fled to Orgrimmar to wait for the crisis to be resolved.
sources: quest 13257 reward text

parts.body: The Horde struck from the ruins with Thrall and Sylvanas at its head. It fought through the courtyard against the traitors' blight, found the lift wrecked and the shaft trapped, and dropped into the inner sanctum on cyclones the Warchief called. Beyond lay the Royal Quarter, where Varimathras opened portals for his demon kin and fell before Thrall and the Dark Lady.

From the sewer entrance, where Broll Bearmantle and Valeera Sanguinar kept watch, King Varian and Jaina Proudmoore led their soldiers down past the engorged blight worm that guarded the tunnels to the Apothecarium. There, among his blight generators, Putress met his end, and Varian declared justice served.

Varian marched in declaring that Putress was only the first strike, and that the time had come to disband the Horde's treacherous kingdom of murderers and thieves. Then he turned his blades on Thrall. Jaina begged him to stop, froze the combatants where they stood and carried the Alliance away. It did not have to be like this, she said. The fellowship of the Wrathgate did not survive the day.

title: The Lady's Necklace
body: Windrunner Spire, on the coast of the Ghostlands, was once the home of the Windrunner family, and of Sylvanas, the Ranger-General who fell defending Quel'Thalas and now rules the Forsaken. Today mindless Scourge haunt its halls. Among them a necklace has turned up, a remarkable piece that shimmers as though the gloom of the Ghostlands cannot touch it. Its inscription names it the lost property of Lady Sylvanas Windrunner herself, and whoever recovers it does best to take it first to High Executor Mavren at Tranquillien, the highest ranking Forsaken in the land, who will know what to do with it.

parts.body: Mavren knew the necklace for what it was: a gift to Lady Sylvanas from her sister, Alleria. It had to go to her at once, to the Royal Quarter where she holds court, by way of the orb of translocation in Silvermoon City that crosses to the Undercity.
sources: quest 9180 description

parts.body: Sylvanas seized it, startled into memory, then mastered herself and scorned the gift. Alleria, she declared, was a long dead memory, and the trinket meant nothing to the queen of the Forsaken. She let it fall and dismissed the bearer. Yet a moment later she knelt and took it up again. Whispering 'Belore', she wove a glamour that called forth Highborne spirits, and the chamber filled with their ancient song of the sin'dorei.

title: The Crown of Will
body: Lady Sylvanas desired the Crown of Will, a relic to be had in Alterac, and sent the ogre Mug'Thol and his warband to fetch it, bound to her service by possession. Mug'Thol found the crown and, being an ogre, could not resist putting it on. Its power let him throw off the Dark Lady's will. She wants an example made, and Sharlindra of the Royal Quarter passes the task to her lieutenant Melisara at Tarren Mill, who means to deal with the ogre quickly, thoroughly and without incident. First the Crushridge, who have overrun the ruins of Alterac under Mug'Thol, must be thinned.

parts.body: The snow of Alterac bloomed red with ogre blood before Melisara was satisfied, and then she wanted heads: those of Targ, Muckrake and Glommus, Mug'Thol's loyal lieutenants. When they were brought to her she promised that his would join them, all four mounted on pikes above Alterac as a monument to those who defy the Dark Lady.
sources: quests 518 and 519 description and reward text

parts.body: Mug'Thol fell at last, and his head and the crown came back to Tarren Mill. His head would adorn the highest peak of the ruins of Alterac, Melisara declared, and the Deathguard would sweep what remained of the Crushridge into the ground.
sources: quest 520 description and reward text

parts.body: The crown itself went back to Sharlindra, to be laid before the queen it was always meant for. She marveled that something so simple could hold such power and fall into such clumsy hands, and promised that Lady Sylvanas would hear who had brought it home.

title: The Deathstalkers
body: Promising rogues of the Horde may find themselves summoned to the Rogues' Quarter by Mennet Carkad, and few ignore the summons, for none care to learn what became of the last who did. Carkad tests candidates for the Deathstalkers, the Dark Lady's elite guard, and he does not pretend the test is safe: it could mean death. He tells the recruit little. First they must obtain the personal effects of Astor Hadren, a messenger who travels between Silverpine and the Undercity, by whatever means suits them. The less the recruit knows of the business the better, Carkad says, but success will earn the rest.

parts.body: Astor's letter of introduction is the key. Carkad's leaders suspect Andron Gant, a merchant whose shop stands by the Apothecarium, of aiding some other power, and they want proof of whom he serves. The recruit is to call on him posing as the messenger he expects. Andron, Carkad judges, lacks the wit to be suspicious.
sources: quest 14419 description
quest 14420 reward text

parts.body: Andron suspected nothing. He welcomed the false messenger, handed over his ledger with his regards and asked that the same courier be sent again. The ledger named his true buyers: the Syndicate. The lords of Alterac, Carkad mused, have fallen far since their betrayal, and with that he welcomed the recruit into the Deathstalkers.

parts.body: The new agent carried the ledger to Aleric Hawkins, master of the Deathstalkers, in the Royal Quarter. Hawkins found the work admirable, commended the recruit's part in it and hoped such service would become routine, for his Deathstalkers always have use for a capable agent.

title: Seeping Corruption
body: In the Apothecarium, Chemist Cuely keeps a patient who did not come to be studied. Thersa Windsong, a tauren, was wounded by naga in the Ruins of Eldarath in Azshara and afterward drank from a tide pool on the beach. She has been sick ever since. No priest or shaman could help her, and she came to the Undercity because its alchemists were said to be studying long and hard on a cure for their own affliction, though the place makes her feel far from welcome. Cuely wants to know what she drank, and has a helper fill labeled vials at the pools.

parts.body: Cuely is pleased the samples came back before she died. He has studied her symptoms with interest, and he is frank about where this leads: she cannot survive, so she might as well die doing something noble for the Forsaken. He brews an elixir from the samples and has it carried to her. Perhaps it will cure her, he says, perhaps not.
sources: quest 3568 completion and reward text
quest 3569 description

parts.body: Thersa finds Cuely disturbingly accommodating, but if he says the elixir will help her, she has no other choice and no time left to find another remedy. She drinks, praying that the Earthmother will watch over her spirit.

title: The Jeremiah Blues
body: Among the records the Forsaken keep, few are stranger than the city census. Royal Overseer Bauhaus tends it by arcane means and disciplined mind, tracking the populace since the city was freed from the Scourge, and he is asked often enough whether someone is dead. When a dusty parcel turned up in the Plaguelands, addressed more than four years earlier to one Jeremiah Felstone of Lordaeron, the census was the place to learn whether its recipient had outlived the plague, and what he had become.

parts.body: The census held the answer. Like some Forsaken, Felstone had shed his old name with his old life, and now sold cockroaches as Jeremiah Payson, groveling under a walkway near the bank. Bauhaus wished the bearer well on so world-shaping an errand.
sources: quest 5023 reward text
quest 5049 description

parts.body: Jeremiah took the visit badly. He had not used the name Felstone in years, and the sender, his sister Janice, had been dead for four. He called the bearer a vulture and threatened to break his own brittle foot on them, until he saw the parcel truly came from her.
sources: quest 5049 reward text

parts.body: Inside lay her personal effects: the deed to the Felstone farm, which he chose not to reclaim, and half of a good luck charm, the other half her husband's. If her spirit still walked the farm unable to rest, he asked, would the bearer return the charm to her, so that knowing he had these things might let her be at peace.
